title: LedgerEvent
description: Something that happened, and who or what did it. An event does not know its place in a ledger: that belongs to the line.

id.description: The identity of the event. The same thing read twice gives the same id.

type.description: What happened. A new type is added to this list, never used without it.

adapter.description: The adapter that read or received it.

kind.description: observed: read from the team's tools. claimed: sent by a session about itself.

project.description: The project the event belongs to.

actor.description: The team member who did it. On a task given or taken back: the one who gave it or took it back. (A task.assigned written before `to` existed names the one who got the task here: read it with assignee.)

id.description: The identity of the team member.

to.description: Only on task.assigned and task.unassigned: the team member the event is about, when that is not the one who did it. On task.assigned: the one who got the task. On task.unassigned: the one it was taken from.

id.description: The identity of the team member.

session.description: For an agent: the session the event comes from.

model.description: For an agent: the model ID of the session.

effort.description: For an agent: the effort of the session.

role.description: For an agent: its role in this session, a name the team chooses (review, build, test, fix ...).

prompt.description: For an agent: the role prompt.

file.description: The file of the role prompt.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the content of the file.

task.description: The task, as the tracker names it.

change.description: The merge or pull request, as the code host names it.

branch.description: The branch of the change or of the working directory.

sig.description: The Ed25519 signature of the event's fixed form without sig, by the key of an assignment (key.issued) or by the issuer.

key.description: The key's id: the SHA-256 of its raw public key.

data.description: What belongs to this type of event only.

mode.description: trial: the ledger serves observation and does not count as evidence.

not.description: `to` stands only where it means something: on a task given or taken back.

activity.description: The types that are activity, not evidence: they go to a file of their own without a chain, and expire. Every one is also in the list of types.
